clock.purpose: The new-tab desk clock only; tabular figures, day period at 0.24em in Dial Grey.

headline.purpose: Full-panel titles (Settings, Bookmarks, Browsing history, Downloads).

headline-column.purpose: Panel titles in the narrow library column.

address-origin.purpose: The host in the address line; the heaviest text in the toolbar.

address.purpose: The editable address and the URL path.

body.purpose: Every control, menu item and tab title; panel explanatory prose capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: Secondary text, form labels, the connection word and shield count.

shadows.name: float

shadows.name: signal-rule
shadows.purpose: Selected tab top edge (3px inset bar in the vertical column, 2px bottom rule on the active Settings section, and 3px insertion-edge rule when dragging tabs).

shadows.name: location-focus
shadows.purpose: Address line focus ring, with a signal border.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, border, colour, opacity and 1px press transitions on controls; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: tab-enter
motion.purpose: Newly opened tab size and opacity entrance; skipped at startup and under reduced motion.

motion.name: loading-slide
motion.purpose: The 2px loading bar; a static full-width bar under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Navigation row wraps; the address line takes its own line; full panels pad 16px.

narrative.overview:
Rust Browser's chrome is an instrument panel for the web: a row of precise, legible
controls whose job is to report state honestly and get out of the way. Every reading
means something. The connection badge says *Encrypted*, *Not encrypted* or *Browser
page* in plain words; the shield shows a number only when it is counting; the loading
bar moves only while a page loads. Nothing on the panel is decoration, and nothing
pretends to know more than it does.

The panel is graphite and restrained: four stacked tonal layers (tab strip, toolbar,
panel, card) separated by hairlines rather than shadows, one typeface family from
Windows itself, and a single **signal** colour per theme that marks what is active,
focused or in progress. The address line is the one bold element; it carries the
site's origin in a heavier display cut so the user always knows where they are. All
else stays quiet so the website, not the browser, is the picture.

The panel has its own look rather than imitating Fluent or Edge, but it is mounted in
a Windows window and respects that window's behaviour: the native title bar, Snap,
Narrator, high contrast, reduced motion and display scaling (checked at 100% and 150%).
Density is compact and desktop-first: 32px controls, 13px text, 4px spacing steps.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite tonal layers and 1px hairlines; shadows only on things that float.
One signal colour per theme, used for state, never for decoration.
The address line is the single emphasised element; the origin is set heavier than the path.
Segoe UI Variable throughout: Display cut for headings and the origin, Text cut for everything else.
Plain-word state readouts over icons alone; every icon button has a name and a shortcut in its tooltip.
Compact desktop density: 32px controls, 13px body, a 4px spacing scale.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Each theme has exactly one signal colour, and it only ever means *active, focused, in progress, private or waiting for your decision*. It never fills a large area at full strength: its biggest solid uses are the 2px loading bar, the selected tab's 2px top rule and the small private label. The one area use is the new-tab **Glow** background, which mixes 10% of the signal into the surface and only when the user chooses Glow.

rules.name: The Theme-Token Rule
rules.body: New surfaces use the theme variables (`--surface`, `--panel`, `--accent`, …), never literal colours, so all five themes and high contrast work without extra code. Website colours never enter the chrome; the new-tab backgrounds Plain, Dusk, Glow and Panels are mixed only from the current theme's own tokens.

rules.name: The Wallpaper Rule
rules.body: The one owner-approved exception ("Drawn + your own", 2026-11-26) to the Theme-Token Rule is the new-tab wallpapers, the only chrome surfaces that carry literal colours. The four drawn wallpapers (Aurora, Dunes, Horizon, Contours) are inline SVG data URLs, each with a dark rendition for Dark, Black, Slate and Plum and a light one for Light; **Your picture** is the user's own PNG, JPEG or WebP from the profile, set as a checked `data:` URL. Every wallpaper sits under washes of `--panel`: a linear wash from 12% at the top to 58% (40% to 72% on Your picture) and a radial hero wash behind the clock, search and caption (62%; 82% on Your picture). On Your picture the date, the clock's day period, the caption and the tile names switch from Dial Grey to the text colour. Together these keep secondary text at 4.5:1 or better (measured: Dark Aurora lowest at 4.55:1, Your picture on Light 7.7:1 and up). High contrast replaces every background with Canvas, and the signal colour never appears in a wallpaper.

rules.name: The Origin-First Rule
rules.body: The site's origin is always the largest emphasised text in the toolbar. Nothing else in the tab strip, navigation row or bookmarks bar may be set at 600 weight and 15px or larger. The selected tab's title keeps regular weight at 13px; selection is marked by colour, surface and the top signal rule, so it never competes with the origin. Headings on full panels such as the library and new tab are below the toolbar and exempt.

rules.name: The Plain Word Rule
rules.body: State is written as a word as well as shown by an icon or colour (*Not encrypted*, a blocked-request count, "Private"), so it survives high contrast, colour blindness and Narrator.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: Only a surface that floats over the page gets a shadow. Cards, buttons, tabs and panels never do.

rules.name: The Live-Page Rule
rules.body: While a dropdown is open, the page behind it stays live and undimmed: video keeps playing and a press on the page closes the dropdown. Over a webpage the toolbar is clipped to the chrome and the dropdown's rounded shape, so the dropdown's own shadow is not drawn there; its Hairline border marks its edge. Over a full panel (the new-tab page, Settings) the panel is dimmed by the menu backdrop scrim.

dos: **Do** use the theme variables for every colour so Dark, Black, Slate, Plum, Light and high contrast all work, and keep their names stable for the contrast tests (the new-tab wallpapers are the one exception; see the Wallpaper Rule).
**Do** keep the signal colour for state: selected, focused, loading, private, active shield, a pending permission decision.
**Do** ask before anything destructive in the browser's confirmation dialog, with Cancel focused and a button that names the action.
**Do** keep permission choices equal in weight, and let only Allow grant: closing or waiting answers Don't allow.
**Do** give every icon-only control an accessible name and put its keyboard shortcut in the tooltip.
**Do** write state in plain words next to its icon or colour (*Not encrypted*, *Private*, a count).
**Do** keep controls 32px tall (34px round navigation buttons, 36px location line) and spacing on the 4px scale.
**Do** draw new icons on the 24px grid with 1.8px round-capped strokes.
**Do** provide a reduced-motion fallback and a forced-colours fallback for every new state cue.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent colour or use the signal for decoration, solid large fills or illustration (the Glow background's 10% tint is the only area use).
**Don't** put shadows on cards, buttons, tabs or panels; only floating dropdowns, menus and the confirmation dialog get the Float shadow.
**Don't** use the error colour for anything that is not a problem or a destructive action.
**Don't** load fonts, images or anything else from a website or a CDN into the chrome; icons are inline SVG and favicons arrive as checked data URLs.
**Don't** freeze or dim the page behind a dropdown; clip the toolbar to the dropdown so the page keeps running.
**Don't** imitate Fluent or Edge controls outright, and don't break Windows behaviour (title bar, Snap, Narrator, scaling) for the sake of the look.
**Don't** set anything else in the toolbar larger than the address origin, or at 600 weight and 15px or more.
